fields.name: app_id
fields.help: app_id issued by the Banggood Open Platform (https://api.banggood.com, Manager Center) after the partner application is approved; calls must come from the registered IP address.

fields.name: app_secret
fields.help: The app_secret. GET /getAccessToken?app_id=&app_secret= returns an access_token valid 2 hours, sent as the access_token query parameter and renewed automatically.

config_fields.name: warehouse
config_fields.help: Banggood warehouse code for quote_shipping (the `warehouse` of GetProductInfo's warehouse_list, e.g. CN, US, UK); the API rejects the call (12031) when it is missing.

config_fields.name: currency
config_fields.help: Currency for prices and shipping fees (e.g. USD); Banggood uses USD when unset.

me.note: No account endpoint; the probe obtains a token and reads the country list ({code: 0, countries[{country_id, country_name}]}), so `account` holds that list.

list_products.note: GET /product/getProductList: `category` (cat_id, a SUB-category id from GetCategoryList) is required by Banggood (12021 otherwise); `query` is not accepted. Pages hold at most 20 products; prices come from get_product (warehouse_list) and not from the list.

get_product.note: GET /product/getProductInfo?product_id=: {product_name, weight (kg), poa_list[{option_name, option_values[{poa_id, poa_name, poa_price}]}], warehouse_list[{warehouse, warehouse_price}], image_list, description}. `price` is the first warehouse's price; the response does not echo the product id, so `id` is empty and the requested id is the product. Pass poa_id and warehouse from here to orders.

quote_shipping.note: GET /product/getShipments: `country` is Banggood's English country NAME (e.g. United States, see GetCountries), not an ISO code; the warehouse comes from the `warehouse` setting. Products with attribute options also need a poa_id, which the vocabulary cannot pass (the API then answers 12033).

get_order.note: GET /order/getOrderInfo?sale_record_id= (YOUR order reference used when the order was imported): the first Banggood order under it {order_id, status, currency, total_amount, sub_amount, shipfee, product_list}; amounts are decimal strings, so they are returned as total_amount rather than the numeric `total`. `id` in the result is Banggood's order_id, which track takes.

track.note: GET /order/getTrackInfo?order_id= (Banggood order_id from get_order): track_info[{event, time (UTC)}], latest and historical events.

not_offered.create_order: POST /order/importOrder is a form post of PHP-style nested arrays (product_list[0][product_id], [warehouse], [poa_id], [shipmethod_code], ... per line, plus product_total; see the official PHP sample https://api.banggood.com/download/banggoodAPI.php.zip); the runtime's form body cannot expand an items array of arbitrary length into indexed bracket keys, and imported orders are then paid in the Banggood web ApiOrderList page.
